description: Flood Inundation Mapper is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USGS, United States Geological Survey; National Weather Service; USACE, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Communities can visualize potential flooding scenarios, identify areas and resources that may be at risk, and enhance their local response effort during a flooding event. Users can explore inundation maps that show where flooding could occur given a selected stream condition. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – General. Assets: Critical Facilities, Energy and Utilities, Property, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
